name: Jessica Killin

summary.text: Jessica Killin is a U.S. Army veteran and attorney who served as a Captain and Military Police Officer, and later worked more than a decade at USAA and as a congressional and White House staffer, including as chief of staff to Second Gentleman Doug Emhoff.
She is a fourth-generation Colorado native, raised in Colorado Springs by two public school educators, and graduated from Falcon High School and Georgetown University's law school.
She is the Democratic nominee for Colorado's 5th Congressional District, challenging incumbent Jeff Crank.

experience.text: Captain and Military Police Officer, U.S. Army, leading soldiers overseas.
Executive, USAA, working on VA home loans and protections for military families, over a decade.
Political staffer to Reps. Donna Shalala (D-Fla.), Carolyn Maloney (D-N.Y.), and Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (D-Wash.), and to Second Gentleman Doug Emhoff.

positions.quote: I will end the harmful tariffs that are driving up prices, which Jeff Crank has repeatedly voted to protect.
I will work to reverse Medicaid cuts that raise healthcare costs and take on drug and insurance companies to lower prescription prices and premiums.

positions.source_title: Where Jeff Crank, Jessica Killin stand on the issues in Colorado's race to represent the 5th Congressional District
positions.quote: She said she would “pull back on or eliminate” tax cuts for large corporations and the wealthy — “those making over $1 million.”
positions.note: Answering which H.R. 1 tax cuts she would keep or change, she would preserve only targeted middle- and lower-income provisions and reverse the law's corporate and top-earner tax cuts; inferred opposition to the law as passed, coded no stronger than disagree since she was not asked squarely whether Congress was right to pass it.

positions.source_title: Where Jeff Crank, Jessica Killin stand on the issues in Colorado's race to represent the 5th Congressional District
positions.quote: There are people who have been caught up in mass deportations who don’t deserve to be sent home, and they should never be deported to a third country, she said.
positions.note: Opposes the scale/methods of current mass-deportation enforcement while also saying she is glad the border is secure, elsewhere in the same answer; coded as a qualified disagree.

positions.source_title: Colorado U.S. House District 5 candidate Q&A
positions.quote: I will fight for harsher penalties on fentanyl traffickers and violent criminals while keeping assault weapons out of the hands of criminals.
positions.note: Supports tougher penalties for fentanyl traffickers but does not specifically address mandatory prison for any amount sold, so coded as a qualified agree rather than the strongest value.
